program.title: Ternary compute: a capability and research horizon
program.goal: Determine whether exact ternary semantics, packed execution, and explicit learning updates can form a useful training/inference engine on ordinary hardware; distribute only workloads with demonstrated value, and admit learned circuits through an independent correctness boundary.

sources.note: Repository operating rules; read before any work. This roadmap does not replace empirical registration or FINDINGS.json.
Existing scalar VM. H00 must pin and recheck it; its presence is not a qualified packed or neural backend.
Existing arithmetic and truth-table semantics; distinguish tritwise clamping from wide neural accumulation.
Existing evidence ledger, not automatically imported as new capability certificates.

Bounded arithmetic, local IPC recovery, and registered controller-only native profiling. Reuse these artifacts under their actual scope; no horizon capability is admitted automatically and actual mini-PC qualification remains open.
Separate switch-level machine design. Its device costs are not CPU timings or energy measurements.
Sibling research entry point; H00 reads the current handoff, journal, system, and relevant artifacts before reusing results.
Existing scientific skill tree; cross-reference it rather than copying its completion labels. This roadmap grants no inherited unlocks.

units.title: Inventory the actual starting point
units.question: Which implementation, evidence, and hardware assets exist now, and which claims are only proposals?

outputs.assessment: A version-pinned inventory with inaccessible or unverified assets explicitly named.
outputs.capability: A reviewed source map and reuse boundary sufficient to identify the exact reference implementation and applicable research protocols.

acceptance: Record repository commits, dirty-tree/file hashes, relevant tests and their actual run status; distinguish code inspection from runtime evidence.
Read the sibling grokking handoff, journal, system, and relevant skill-tree entries; distinguish committed results, ignored raw data, and narrative claims.
Identify existing VM neural-task benchmarks and any related aethor transport work without adopting its security claims or changing that repository.
Record the mini-PC fleet as user-reported until individually inventoried; no network discovery outside explicitly supplied machines.
units.falsifier: An asset is treated as implemented or revalidated when only prose, an old run, or an unavailable file supports it.
alternatives: Reuse a qualified existing artifact with a pinned scope.
Reproduce a missing qualification locally.
Leave an inaccessible claim unverified and exclude it from downstream assumptions.

scope.resources: Local read-only inventory and bounded existing checks; no remote jobs.

units.title: Freeze workloads, comparisons, and stopping rules
units.question: What useful result would justify this engine, and what comparison could reject it?

outputs.assessment: An explicit workload and comparison design, including objections.
outputs.capability: A reviewed evaluation contract naming task quality, latency/throughput, memory, budgets, uncertainty, and stopping criteria before measurement.

acceptance: Select a bounded algebraic/generalization task and a practical inference task with accessible data, fixed splits, and justified quality tolerances.
Compare against a competent conventional model and optimized integer implementation, not only the JavaScript interpreter or FP32 storage arithmetic.
Separate weight-only ternary models from models with ternary activations; account for wider accumulators, scaling, normalization, and learning state.

Freeze shape and batch sweeps, seeds, repetition and uncertainty policy, end-to-end cost boundary, and a minimum worthwhile gain; obtain user input only for material use-case, budget, or data choices that remain unresolved.
units.falsifier: The criteria can be changed after seeing results, omit a strong baseline, or cannot distinguish useful improvement from measurement noise.
alternatives: Small classifier or sequence model.
Exact algebraic/circuit tasks with held-out structure.
Reject a proposed workload if data access or the required quality cannot be assessed.

scope.resources: Design and source research only; training budgets are not granted by this unit.

units.title: Specify numerical and state semantics
units.question: What exactly must every backend compute, including the cases a ternary label hides?

outputs.assessment: An arithmetic/state design and an explicit list of incompatible alternatives.
outputs.capability: A reviewed versioned contract for trits, wide accumulators, overflow, rounding, thresholds, bias, reset, and deterministic state transitions.

acceptance: Define valid trits and dual-rail encoding, reject the invalid rail combination, and specify empty dimensions, padding and malformed inputs.
Derive accumulator ranges from shapes and bias bounds; choose explicit overflow behavior and account for values beyond a VM tryte.
Distinguish a scalar ternary value, a multi-trit integer, and a tensor element; do not substitute tritwise CSUM for an unrestricted dot product.
Declare which operations existing VM instructions implement and which require multiword code or a separate typed extension; preserve existing VM behavior.
units.falsifier: Two conforming backends could disagree because an overflow, tie, threshold, precision, or state-boundary rule is unspecified.
alternatives: Fixed-width integer accumulators with checked bounds.
Multiword balanced-ternary accumulation.
Explicit saturating arithmetic as a different, versioned operator contract.

scope.resources: Specification and hand-checkable examples; no ISA change implicitly authorized.

units.title: Design target-machine and physical-network measurement
units.question: How will measurements on the actual mini PCs and their offline links be made comparable and safe?

outputs.assessment: A hardware inventory template, wiring plan, and measurement limitations.
outputs.capability: A reviewed procedure for identifying the execution host, CPU features, core topology, NICs, storage, thermals, and available power instrumentation.

acceptance: Treat the reported Ryzen fleet and RAM as an inventory target, not confirmed identical machines; record CPUID/features, firmware, OS, memory and NIC details when access exists.
Plan a dedicated Ethernet switch and controller interface; specify addressing and intentional absence of Internet routing or bridging. Offline Ethernet is still a network.
Distinguish physical cores and SMT siblings; prepare single-core, physical-core and SMT comparisons without assuming scaling.
Define warmup, sustained duration, affinity, frequency/thermal reporting, and whether energy comes from a wall meter, package estimate, or is unavailable; do not infer joules from gate counts.
units.falsifier: A timing lacks its actual host/thermal context, or a network isolation or energy claim exceeds what the proposed instrument can observe.
alternatives: Existing minimal Linux for the first pilot.
Later immutable appliance if operational measurements justify it.
Single-node operation while physical access or network details are unresolved.

scope.resources: Inventory/wiring instructions only; no disk flashing, interface reconfiguration, or remote access.

units.title: Qualify an independent exact scalar oracle
units.question: Can a simple independent implementation expose mistakes shared by the VM and optimized kernels?

outputs.assessment: A reproducible correctness report, including counterexamples.
outputs.capability: A qualified exact scalar oracle on a declared domain, with powered checks and an explicit VM compatibility boundary.

acceptance: Check the complete scalar product truth table, hand-derived edge cases, and an exhaustively enumerated small-vector domain.
Use an independently formulated reduction rather than copying the packed equations into both subject and oracle.
Compare applicable operations against the current VM, including multiword or overflow refusal behavior.
Break the implementation deliberately in isolated test fixtures and require checks to detect sign, zero, carry, threshold and overflow defects; report sampled versus exhaustive coverage.
units.falsifier: A mismatch, an untested arithmetic boundary, or a deliberate implementation mutation that the check fails to detect.
alternatives: BigInt exact reference for bounded tests.
Range-proved integer reference.
Independent multi-trit interpreter with explicit state bounds.

scope.resources: Bounded local correctness tests; no throughput conclusion.

units.title: Define a portable packed operator interface
units.question: Can independently written backends consume the same unambiguous jobs and data?

outputs.assessment: A representation/interface proposal and compatibility tests.
outputs.capability: A frozen operator and serialization contract with fixtures, validation rules, layout identifiers and resource limits.

acceptance: Specify element order, rail order, byte order, shapes, lengths, alignment assumptions, tail masks and canonical serialization.
Distinguish feature-packed reduction from independent-example bit lanes; no lane-count calculation may count both at once.
Name tensor, circuit and VM boundaries, versioning, deterministic seeds where applicable, and maximum input/output sizes.
Provide scalar fixtures, round-trip checks, and malformed-input refusal cases that both native and JavaScript implementations can consume.
units.falsifier: A producer and consumer can interpret the same byte string differently or accept an invalid rail, shape or tail.
alternatives: Dual-rail masks.
Byte-per-trit interchange with packing internal to a backend.
Separate versioned formats where a single format imposes excessive conversion cost.

scope.resources: Local contract fixtures; interface integration requires the owner of affected files.

units.title: Build a correctness-first measurement harness
units.question: Can the harness distinguish arithmetic correctness, kernel speed, and useful end-to-end improvement?

outputs.assessment: A harness qualification report and identified blind spots.
outputs.capability: A reproducible harness whose controls detect wrong answers and whose measurements retain raw distributions and complete cost boundaries.

acceptance: Refuse performance qualification when correctness checks fail; retain compiler options, source hashes, host identity and run order.
Report prepacked kernel timings separately from packing, allocation, dispatch, reduction, activation and serialization-inclusive timings.
Test that a deliberately wrong implementation fails and that meaningful extra work changes the measured quantity; include healthy controls.
Support matched randomized run order, warmup, sustained tests, uncertainty, resource caps and explicit unavailable metrics; preregister comparative claims before measuring them.
units.falsifier: The harness can report a win for wrong arithmetic, unaccounted work, a dead-code-eliminated computation, or a difference within unresolved noise.
alternatives: In-process native measurements with consumed checksums.
Whole-job subprocess measurements.
Separate kernel and service-level instruments with a shared provenance record.

scope.resources: Bounded local instrument tests; target-machine campaigns need a separate registration and resource allocation.

units.title: Build the strong native integer baseline
units.question: How much can ordinary compiled arithmetic achieve before attributing any benefit to bit slicing?

outputs.assessment: A baseline implementation and correctness review, including failures.
outputs.capability: An exact native integer backend with documented compiler/vectorization choices and identical operator semantics.

acceptance: Implement the complete declared operator using appropriate integer arithmetic, avoiding deliberately weak scalar code when compiler vectorization is available.
Match the oracle and malformed-input behavior on the declared qualification domain.
Separate interpreter overhead from representation effects; record wider accumulator and conversion costs.
Expose the same backend interface and output fixtures used by packed candidates.
units.falsifier: The baseline is incorrect or handicapped in a way that makes a representation comparison misleading.
alternatives: Compiler-vectorized byte/integer arithmetic.
Explicit ordinary SIMD where justified.
A suitable existing native kernel with compatible semantics and dependency approval.

scope.resources: Local compilation and correctness tests; no dependency installation assumed.

units.title: Build the feature-packed candidate
units.question: Can rail logic plus reductions implement the operator efficiently when bits index features?

outputs.assessment: A candidate and correctness/cost limitations, even if unsuitable.
outputs.capability: A qualified feature-packed backend on its declared CPU feature set and shape domain.

acceptance: Implement positive and negative product masks with exact counts and wide accumulation.
Cover invalid rails, partial words, zero dimensions, extreme signs, long reductions and output thresholds.
Offer a portable word path and only supported instruction paths; AVX2 population counting needs an explicit implementation choice.
Report register pressure, conversion and reduction work rather than equating packed values with completed neurons.
units.falsifier: A mismatch, wrong tail count, silent accumulator overflow, unsupported instruction path, or unsupported constant-time whole-layer claim.
alternatives: Scalar machine-word population counts.
AVX2 vectorized counting/reduction.
Ordinary integer arithmetic when packing costs dominate.

scope.resources: Local compilation and correctness tests; target timings belong to H10.

units.title: Build the independent-example bit-sliced candidate
units.question: When each bit is a separate example, can a shared circuit beat feature-packed or ordinary integer execution?

outputs.assessment: An independent-example layout implementation or an evidenced rejection of the candidate.
outputs.capability: A qualified batch-bit-sliced backend with explicit per-example accumulator bitplanes and state separation.

acceptance: Specify how weights broadcast, state belongs to each lane, and wider per-example sums are represented.
Check lane independence and permutation behavior against the oracle, including partial batches and inactive lanes.
Charge transpose/packing, carry or reduction circuitry, register spills and output extraction.
Use whole independent batches per worker; do not insert inter-core or inter-node barriers after individual gates.
units.falsifier: Cross-lane contamination, an omitted accumulator plane, or a claimed throughput that omits required packing or carry work.
alternatives: Boolean adder trees over bitplanes.
Fused fixed-circuit execution for stable shapes.
Reject this layout for divergent or too-small batches.

scope.resources: Local correctness work; independent of H08, with no shared source edits.

units.title: Measure and select layouts without assuming a packed winner
units.question: Which qualified implementation wins for which shapes once the full operator cost is counted?

outputs.assessment: A preregistered comparison with all candidates, failures, uncertainty and raw results.
outputs.capability: A reviewed backend selection policy using only correctness-qualified candidates, including the native baseline when packed variants lose.

acceptance: Register shape, batch, sparsity and data-residency comparisons and the decision policy before timing.
Exclude candidates that lack actual correctness qualification; an assessment port is permission to consider the result, not permission to execute an incorrect kernel.
Report raw and end-to-end costs, confidence/uncertainty, CPU feature dispatch and out-of-domain fallback.
Publish negative and mixed outcomes; make a selection capability mean a valid measured choice, not a declaration that bit slicing won.
units.falsifier: Selection favors an unqualified candidate, hides a losing workload, or relies on an unresolved timing difference.
alternatives: One fixed backend for simplicity.
A measured shape-dependent dispatcher.
Keep ordinary integer execution and close the packed-speed hypothesis for this domain.

scope.resources: One registered target-CPU campaign with declared thermal and wall-time limits; no fleet rollout.

units.title: Execute a complete layer and model path
units.question: Does a correctness-qualified backend remain correct when products become a complete neural computation?

outputs.assessment: An integration report for full layers and supported model paths.
outputs.capability: An exact qualified inference path including accumulation, bias, activation, layout conversion, model loading and output interpretation.

acceptance: Compare intermediate accumulators and final outputs against the scalar contract, not only class labels.
Account for every wider or floating auxiliary operation; describe a hybrid path honestly if one is needed.
Bind model and operator versions, shape limits and deterministic replay fixtures, including the exact backend capability attempt selected for integration.

Include a representative full inference path; a multiplication microbenchmark cannot satisfy this unit. Correctness integration may precede H10 performance selection; it does not substitute for that selection.
units.falsifier: An intermediate mismatch, uncounted conversion, or unsupported layer silently changes model semantics.
alternatives: Fully ternary-activation model with integer thresholds.
Mixed-precision model with explicitly charged boundary operators.
A narrowly supported model family instead of a general neural framework.

scope.resources: Bounded local model fixtures; no claims about useful quality or fleet throughput.

units.title: Test useful model quality independently of speed
units.question: Does the chosen ternary representation retain enough task quality to be worth accelerating?

outputs.assessment: A registered quality comparison with model/data hashes and unsuccessful seeds retained.
outputs.capability: A model meeting the frozen task-quality criterion, with an explicit inference/export contract and total state inventory.

acceptance: Compare appropriate conventional, weight-ternary and strict ternary-activation candidates under the frozen data and budget contract.
Keep held-out evaluation separate from tuning; report uncertainty, seed spread and training compute.
Record optimizer/shadow-weight precision, scales, normalization and accumulators instead of calling the entire training system ternary from its weights alone.
Verify exported forward outputs on reference fixtures before handing a model to the execution lane.
units.falsifier: The representation misses its quality tolerance, validation data influences selection improperly, or hidden wider state invalidates the stated comparison.
alternatives: Train conventional models then evaluate quantization.
Quantization-aware training with wider update state.
Reject a workload where strict ternary activations are not useful.

scope.repo: ternary-grokking for campaigns; tryte-vm for export fixtures
scope.resources: Registered bounded training allocation only; use the owning repository's compute queue and thermal rules.

units.title: Qualify the exact candidate-admission boundary
units.question: What independent evidence permits an optimized or learned implementation to replace an exact one?

outputs.assessment: An admission design with powered refusal cases and scope limits.
outputs.capability: An independent checker that binds a candidate, contract, declared domain and correctness evidence, rejecting missing or mismatched qualification.

acceptance: Select exhaustive finite checking, an appropriate equivalence proof, or a clearly labeled sampled-only research result; sampled agreement never qualifies an unrestricted exact claim.
Bind certificates to candidate/code hashes and arithmetic/domain versions; invalidate them when their inputs change.
Demonstrate rejection of a wrong candidate, stale certificate, malformed shape and plausible sampled impostor on its counterexample.
Keep learned models and candidate generators outside the authority path. A signed receipt authenticates its issuer and content, not computation correctness.
units.falsifier: An incorrect, stale, out-of-domain or merely self-asserted candidate is admitted for an exact claim.
alternatives: Exhaustive checking on deliberately small domains.
SAT/SMT or other independently checked equivalence evidence for a supported circuit language.
Research-only sampled agreement with exact replacement withheld.

scope.resources: Bounded local defensive qualification; no generic untrusted native-code execution service.

units.title: Single-mini-PC useful-computation gate
units.question: Does the engine deliver the predeclared useful improvement on an actual target mini PC?

outputs.assessment: A go/no-go report tying measured quality, full inference cost, memory and sustained behavior to a named machine.
outputs.capability: A useful, exactly qualified workload that meets the frozen quality and improvement criteria on the target hardware.

acceptance: If H11 lacks a qualified inference path or H12 misses model quality, record an evidenced no-go assessment without pretending unrun measurements occurred. A positive capability requires both qualifications to remain valid.

Measure complete inference against the frozen strong baseline only on a qualified path, including loading/packing where the workload requires them. Bind the measured backend to H10's selection and H11's qualified path; never combine one executable's correctness with another's timing.
Compare one core, physical-core workers and SMT workers with recorded affinity and sustained thermal behavior; report all measured crossover points.
Claim energy improvement only with a stated instrument and boundary; otherwise leave energy open. Bind the go decision to its exact model, shapes, host and software.
units.falsifier: Quality, correctness, sustained performance or the minimum worthwhile gain fails the predeclared criterion.
alternatives: Proceed with the demonstrated packed route.
Retain the ordinary integer backend and revise the acceleration hypothesis.
Stop this deployment branch while preserving useful semantics and negative findings.

scope.resources: One supplied mini PC and a bounded registered campaign; no assumed access or fleet changes.

units.title: Define one runtime for prediction and learning
units.question: Can training and inference share explicit state-transition semantics without hiding the extra work of learning?

outputs.assessment: A shared-runtime design and its precision/state tradeoffs.
outputs.capability: A versioned prediction/update contract specifying feedback, learning state, randomness, reset, checkpoint, update order and frozen-state inference.

acceptance: Define predict(state,input) and update(state,input,feedback) or an equivalent explicit mode; no hidden state mutation during frozen inference.
Inventory parameters, accumulators, optimizer/shadow state, RNG and normalizer state with their actual precision.
State determinism boundaries, including parallel reduction and replay order, and specify restart equivalence.
Keep shared-runtime unification separate from the hypothesis that all learning state can be ternary.
units.falsifier: Training-time prediction and frozen inference can disagree without an explicit state/mode distinction, or update state is omitted from accounting.
alternatives: Wider optimizer state with ternary forward execution.
Integer/local-learning rules.
Inference-only runtime with training external if integration is not worthwhile.

scope.resources: Specification and bounded replay fixtures, independent of fleet rollout.

units.title: Demonstrate learning in the shared runtime
units.question: Does the shared engine actually learn, and does freezing updates produce the same inference behavior?

outputs.assessment: A registered learning/replay comparison including all update-state costs and failures.
outputs.capability: A bounded demonstrated training-and-inference engine meeting the selected learning criterion with exact frozen-forward and checkpoint replay checks.

acceptance: Implement a declared update rule and compare with an independent conventional/reference training path under matched data and budget.
Show actual held-out learning, not only deterministic replay or a falling training loss; retain no-learning and shuffled-label controls where appropriate.
Check frozen forward outputs and interrupted/resumed state trajectories within the declared determinism contract.
Report training and inference time separately and include optimizer, gradients or discrete update counters in memory accounting.
units.falsifier: The learner misses its registered criterion, frozen outputs diverge, restart changes the promised trajectory, or hidden state invalidates the cost comparison.
alternatives: Quantization-aware training with wider state.
Local integer learning with a matched baseline.
Keep an external trainer and export qualified inference models.

scope.repo: tryte-vm implementation; ternary-grokking campaign if appropriate
scope.resources: Explicit bounded training allocation; no background training implied.

units.title: Test the fully discrete learning hypothesis
units.question: Can a declared discrete update rule retain useful learning without wider floating optimizer state?

outputs.assessment: A registered discrete-versus-hybrid comparison, including a useful negative result.
outputs.capability: A discrete learning rule meeting the frozen quality and resource criteria on its named task family, with every state width disclosed.

acceptance: Distinguish trit-only parameters from integer counters and genuinely trit-only total state; name exactly which hypothesis is tested.
Compare against the best available hybrid/reference training outcome at matched budgets and data, not a deliberately weak learner.
Register update rule, thresholds, randomization, seed schedule and stopping criteria before observing comparative learning curves.
Keep a refutation local to the tested rule/task; failure does not refute shared-runtime training or all discrete learning.
units.falsifier: The chosen discrete rule fails its quality/resource target or relies on undisclosed wider state.
alternatives: Integer counters with ternary weights.
Strict finite-state update rules.
Retain hybrid learning when it is demonstrably better.

scope.resources: Separately registered bounded campaign; optional to deployment.

units.title: Specify typed circuits as executable artifacts
units.question: What must a found circuit contain to be checked, lowered, and executed independently of its discoverer?

outputs.assessment: A circuit-language proposal and its expressivity/verification tradeoffs.
outputs.capability: A typed bounded circuit IR with exact scalar execution, state boundaries, canonical identity and declared lowering limits.

acceptance: Specify inputs, outputs, wire types, state, supported operators and operation/resource bounds.
Separate combinational acyclic circuits from explicit state-transition loops; do not infer unlimited execution from a finite graph.
Provide known-circuit fixtures, invalid-graph refusals, canonical serialization and reference interpretation.
Keep the research dependency DAG distinct from the circuit being researched.
units.falsifier: A circuit's interpretation depends on undocumented ordering, state, arithmetic, or an unbounded execution path.
alternatives: Combinational Boolean/ternary netlists.
Typed straight-line integer operators.
Explicit bounded state machines as a separate language version.

scope.resources: Local specification and fixtures; no autonomous synthesis campaign.

units.title: Lower known circuits before learned circuits
units.question: Can the proposed circuit interface reach a declared qualified backend without losing semantics or hiding its costs?

outputs.assessment: A known-circuit lowering report including unsupported cases.
outputs.capability: A qualified lowering path for a declared circuit subset with semantic evidence and resource accounting.

acceptance: Use hand-constructed known-correct circuits as controls before any learned candidate is available.

Check reference versus lowered execution within the declared proof/exhaustive boundary and pin the actual selected backend capability attempt. Native-target success does not qualify an untested packed target.

Report emitted operations, temporary storage, spills where measurable, packing, dispatch and synchronization. Correctness lowering may precede H10 performance selection, and is not evidence of a speed advantage.
Preserve a scalar fallback and refuse circuits outside the supported subset.
units.falsifier: A known circuit lowers incorrectly, an unsupported circuit is silently accepted, or logical size is presented as measured execution speed.
alternatives: Ahead-of-time generated native code.
A bounded packed interpreter.
A supported subset with reference execution for the remainder.

scope.resources: Local correctness and instrumentation qualification; no untrusted arbitrary binary deployment.

units.title: Preregister the grokking-to-circuit question
units.question: What observation would distinguish delayed generalization and useful circuit discovery from ordinary fitting or direct search?

outputs.assessment: An attackable experiment design and literature/reuse inventory.
outputs.capability: A preregistration with fixed task family, holdouts, seeds, budgets, controls, extraction method, metrics and falsifiers, durably recorded before runs.

acceptance: Separate training fit, held-out accuracy, structural out-of-distribution behavior, delayed generalization, circuit extraction and exact equivalence.
Include conventional synthesis/optimization and appropriate learning baselines at declared cost; review relevant primary literature before any novelty claim.
Name the grokking criterion and extraction/admission boundary in advance, with powered controls and all failed seeds retained.
Record scientific claims in the owning grokking journal/protocol; this roadmap is only the dependency index.
units.falsifier: The design cannot distinguish the favored mechanism from a matched alternative, or the headline criterion is chosen retrospectively.
alternatives: Learn bounded algebraic maps and extract circuits.
Compare learning-guided proposals with direct synthesis.
Reject the grokking label while still evaluating useful learned optimization.

scope.resources: Design only; execution requires the registered resource budget and owning queue.

units.title: Run the bounded discovery campaign
units.question: Does the registered procedure produce generalization evidence or extractable circuits beyond its controls?

outputs.assessment: The complete registered campaign result, including absent grokking, failed seeds and no-candidate outcomes.
outputs.capability: At least one extracted candidate plus the declared generalization evidence; this output does not itself certify circuit correctness or speed.

acceptance: Run only the registered seeds/tasks/budget, with checkpoints and raw learning curves bound to code/data versions.
Report each registered prediction separately and preserve failed or invalid attempts.
Evaluate structural holdouts without tuning on them, and keep extraction cost separate from inference cost.
Export candidates in the typed circuit format and state exactly which properties remain for independent admission.
units.falsifier: The declared generalization or extraction criterion fails, controls match the effect, or provenance cannot establish what actually ran.
alternatives: Useful extractable candidates.
Generalization without useful extraction.
A bounded negative result followed by a separately registered successor question.

scope.resources: Governed bounded compute; no autonomous budget expansion or unapproved remote jobs.

units.title: Admit and benchmark discovered circuits
units.question: Does any extracted candidate remain exact and useful after real lowering and execution?

outputs.assessment: An admission/execution comparison or an explicit no-candidate conclusion.
outputs.capability: A hash-bound independently admitted discovered circuit with measured improvement over the frozen conventional alternatives on a stated domain.

acceptance: If H21 produced no usable candidate or H19 no qualified lowering path, conclude that explicitly without pretending an execution comparison occurred; positive capability requires both qualifications to remain valid.
Qualify each candidate independently, then compare executed cost including lowering, packing, temporaries and amortized discovery cost where relevant.
Keep exactness domain, learned generalization domain and timing workload separate in every claim.
Preserve rejected candidates and counterexamples; a smaller gate count alone cannot unlock this capability.
units.falsifier: Any required equivalence check fails, the execution gain misses the registered threshold, or a sampled-only result is promoted to exact replacement.
alternatives: Admit a narrow useful circuit.
Keep a candidate as sampled-only research evidence.
Retain the conventional circuit and close the tested learned-speed hypothesis.

scope.resources: Bounded independent checks and target timings; no production authority replacement without this gate.

units.title: Specify bounded distributed jobs and result acceptance
units.question: Can offline workers execute independent jobs while identity, retries and result correctness remain separate claims?

outputs.assessment: A worker/protocol design with explicit trust and failure boundaries.
outputs.capability: A frozen bounded job contract covering identities, model/code hashes, resources, retries, checkpoints, cancellation and result-admission rules.

acceptance: Use whole circuits/models on independent batches or independent experiments; no per-gate synchronization across Ethernet.
Define logical job and attempt identities, pre-provisioned peer identity, result binding, replay handling, and at-most-once acceptance despite potentially repeated execution.
Separate authentication, computation checking and boot measurement/attestation; document which are implemented and which are merely self-reported.
Enumerate existing secure transport reuse versus a separately reviewed custom channel; choose no custom cryptographic primitive and assume offline peers can still fail or be compromised.
units.falsifier: A stale/mismatched result can be accepted, retries double-count work, or a signature/HELLO is treated as computation proof or trusted measured boot.
alternatives: Existing authenticated transport with explicit job framing.
An existing project channel only after its exact trust properties are qualified.
Local process workers before network distribution.

scope.repo: tryte-vm design; any aethor integration needs its own scoped work order
scope.resources: Protocol design only; no VM API operations, firewall changes or remote deployments.

units.title: Qualify a two-node pilot
units.question: Do already-useful independent jobs gain from distribution and recover correctly from worker-process failures?

outputs.assessment: A registered local-versus-network pilot with recovery and scaling findings.
outputs.capability: A bounded distributed worker pilot with qualified job acceptance, repeatable outputs and a measured useful operating range.

acceptance: Use the same qualified jobs locally and on supplied workers; measure data transfer, scheduling and checking cost separately from computation.
Test duplicate delivery, timeout, cancellation, worker-process exit, restart and partial-result recovery using test-owned processes.
Demonstrate at-most-once logical acceptance and deterministic outputs under the stated state/seed contract.
Measure compute-to-network ratio and controller overhead; stop expansion if distribution misses the registered usefulness criterion.
units.falsifier: Wrong/duplicate acceptance, unrecoverable authorized process failure, nondeterministic promised outputs, or network overhead erases the required benefit.
alternatives: Batch inference over resident models.
Independent training seeds/search jobs.
Continue single-node operation if jobs are too small or stateful.

scope.resources: Two explicitly supplied workers; approved configuration and test-owned process interruption only.

units.title: Qualify the worker appliance and recovery path
units.question: Does a minimal reproducible worker image improve operation without breaking drivers, recovery, or observability?

outputs.assessment: A baseline-Linux versus appliance qualification and a recovery runbook.
outputs.capability: A reproducible worker image and rollback/reprovisioning procedure qualified on the pilot hardware.

acceptance: Compare an existing minimal Linux setup with an immutable image option such as Buildroot; a custom kernel is not assumed necessary.
Qualify NIC, storage, CPU feature state, thermal observation, identity provisioning and deterministic job behavior.
Bind image/build inputs and distinguish image identity from remote attestation; read-only root alone is not execution determinism.
Test reboot/recovery on approved devices and preserve a rollback image. Disk replacement or flashing requires an explicit device-specific approval before action.
units.falsifier: Missing drivers, inaccessible thermals, unrecoverable provisioning, lost identity, or claims that immutability proves correct execution.
alternatives: Minimal conventional Linux appliance.
Reproducible immutable Buildroot image.
Keep the pilot OS if a custom image adds no demonstrated operational value.

scope.repo: tryte-vm appliance prototype or a separately approved systems repository
scope.resources: Pilot devices only; physical installation and reboot scope approved separately.

units.title: Measure fleet scaling before declaring a mesh advantage
units.question: Does the reported fleet improve useful throughput under sustained, fault-tolerant operation?

outputs.assessment: A registered scaling curve and bottleneck report across available fleet sizes.
outputs.capability: A fleet configuration with measured useful scaling, bounded recovery behavior and declared operational limits.

acceptance: Scale incrementally from the pilot toward the available fleet, validating each machine rather than assuming uniform hardware.
Report throughput, latency, controller load, network bytes, stragglers, memory residence and sustained thermals; report wall energy only if measured.
Distinguish embarrassingly parallel training seeds from synchronized distributed training; model-update communication is a separate experiment.
Retain unsuccessful scale points and stop at the measured economical configuration; installed RAM and packed lane counts are not throughput evidence.
units.falsifier: Additional machines miss the usefulness criterion, reliability degrades, or resource/thermal constraints invalidate the sustained result.
alternatives: Full available fleet for independent jobs.
A smaller efficient worker pool.
Dedicated roles for training seeds, inference batches or verification, justified by measurements.

scope.resources: Only individually approved worker hosts and bounded campaigns; no new purchases assumed.

units.title: Make the first portfolio decision
units.question: After the single-node answer, which parts deserve continued investment and which should stop?

outputs.assessment: A decision record that names supported, refuted and open claims, including blocked downstream work.
outputs.capability: A reviewed next-stage allocation and scope decision grounded in the current evidence, not a blanket approval of every branch.

acceptance: Accept a negative single-node result as a completed answer; do not wait for deployment descendants that now cannot start.
Review available learning/discovery/system evidence without inventing missing results; explicitly state which branches remain independent and worth testing.
Choose continue, narrow, pivot or stop with mechanism-level reasons and a falsifiable next question.
Record revised work as successor units/contracts and explicit resolution notes; preserve old attempts and never erase a failed claim by relabeling it.
units.falsifier: A failed gate is silently bypassed, a blocked branch is presented as complete, or a revision hides the result that motivated it.
alternatives: Continue deployment after a useful single-node result.
Keep only the reference/learning research lane.
Stop this acceleration direction and bank its reusable instruments and failures.

scope.resources: Evidence synthesis only; new budgets or deployments need their own allocation.

units.title: Integrate the useful training/inference appliance
units.question: Do the independently qualified pieces form an operable end-to-end engine?

outputs.assessment: An integration/reproduction report with residual limitations and operational cost.
outputs.capability: A versioned, reproducible bounded training/inference appliance with qualified distributed jobs, reference checks and recovery documentation.

acceptance: Re-run end-to-end quality, correctness, performance and recovery checks on the combined versions; component success alone is insufficient.
Publish an operator/model support matrix, resource envelopes and deterministic replay limits.
Have a different model/operator reproduce setup and a bounded job from the handoff without undocumented intervention.
Keep learned-circuit adoption optional and separately certified; neither full discrete learning nor grokking is required to operate the basic engine.
units.falsifier: Integration changes semantics, loses a required quality/performance result, or cannot be reproduced and recovered from the written handoff.
alternatives: Qualified shared training/inference appliance.
Narrower inference-only or single-node release via an explicit successor contract.
Retain a research prototype if operational obligations remain unmet.

scope.repo: tryte-vm and already qualified systems components
scope.resources: Bounded acceptance jobs on approved hosts; no public release or external service deployment implied.

units.title: Synthesize the scientific frontier claim
units.question: What was learned about discrete learning, generalization and executable circuit discovery beyond existing methods?

outputs.assessment: A source-backed scientific synthesis, including null results and unresolved mechanisms.
outputs.capability: A reproducible research report with independently reviewed claim scope, comparison to primary prior art and an explicit next falsifier.

acceptance: Separate observed delayed generalization, proposed mechanism, exact circuit equivalence, and actual execution advantage.
Compare with relevant current primary research and direct synthesis/optimization; no frontier or novelty label follows from local success alone.
Preserve seed distributions, unsuccessful tasks, extraction failures, proof boundaries and discovery amortization costs.
State the strongest supported claim and the nearest observation that would break it; a well-powered negative result is eligible for this report.
units.falsifier: The synthesis promotes a finite or sampled result to universality, ignores a competitive baseline, or presents a hypothesis as an established mechanism.
alternatives: A positive bounded research result.
A useful boundary or negative result.
An inconclusive report that identifies the missing discriminating instrument.

scope.repo: ternary-grokking scientific record; tryte-vm roadmap links
scope.resources: Analysis and independent review; publication or new experiments are separate actions.
